claims.exact_statement: If a universal KLS/Poincare bound C_P(mu) <= C0 ||Cov(mu)||_op holds for all log-concave mu, then for isotropic compactly supported log-concave p on R^d, a C1 map chi:R^d->R^k with bounded partial derivatives, E_p chi=0, q=chi_*p isotropic, and G8=(E_p||grad chi||_op^8)^(1/2)<infinity, the Brownian-transport proof yields E_q||tau_q||_HS^2 <= C_* min(d,k)(log(ed))^8 G8 and W2^2(Law(n^-1/2 sum_{j=1}^n Y_j),N(0,I_k)) <= C_*[min(d,k)(log(ed))^8 G8+k]/n for iid Y_j~q. For every integer m>=1 it also yields E_gamma||D X_t||^(2m) <= C_*^m(2m+1)!(log(ed))^(4m), uniformly 0<=t<=1. C_* may depend on C0 and universal constants in the inherited Brownian-transport estimates, but is dimension independent and not numerically extracted.
assumptions: Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec arXiv:2610.05474v1 KLS claim is correct (source-reported only in this audit).

Mikulincer-Shenfeld Brownian-transport estimates and stochastic-calculus proof chain are valid with the selected positive exponent kappa=1/log(d); source dimension d>=3, with log(ed) absorbing small dimensions.
p is isotropic, log-concave, compactly supported; chi is continuously differentiable with bounded partial derivatives; q is centered and isotropic; G8 finite.

claims.novelty_boundary: KLS concentration, Poincare/isoperimetry, sampling, volume, and the identity/linear-image CLT are routine consequences or prior results. Mikulincer-Shenfeld already prove the nonlinear pushforward Stein-kernel/CLT interface and explicitly note that KLS would improve transport moments up to logarithmic factors. Re-running their proof changes the displayed log loss from (log d)^24 to (log d)^8 and preserves a min(d,k) rank factor seen in the proof, but this is source-anticipated and is not a new compositional CLT. Their displayed compact-support theorem also does not itself cover genuinely heavy-tailed pushforwards.

acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.exact_sampler_model: Given an exact iid sampler for p and an evaluable chi, n output samples require n p draws, n chi evaluations, O(nk) output-coordinate arithmetic, and O(k) streaming memory. The comparison Gaussian needs k normal variates once q mean/covariance normalization is supplied. The W2 theorem is distributional and supplies no explicit sample-to-Gaussian coupling algorithm.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.density_support_oracle: No sampler is supplied. Hit-and-run or another sampler must separately charge density/line-restriction integration, warm-start ratio M, convex-body geometry, and finite-precision error. KLS improves a conductance premise but such sampling consequences are prior art and not a novel result here.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.normalization_conditioning: Center and whiten q. If output covariance Sigma_q is supplied and lambda_min(Sigma_q)>0, whitening gives G8( Sigma_q^(-1/2)(chi-Echi),p ) <= lambda_min(Sigma_q)^(-2) G8(chi,p). Reduce to the covariance support rank when q is singular. Estimating/certifying the mean and covariance has additional data/sample costs not included in the theorem.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.moment_acquisition: G8 must have an analytic or certified upper bound; a finite empirical moment estimate alone does not certify it absent tail assumptions. Compact support and a bound on chi derivatives/images are needed for concrete ranges.
acquisition_oracle_geometry_conditioning.finite_precision: If each transformed summand has deterministic Euclidean error <= delta_chi, normalized-sum error is <= sqrt(n) delta_chi. If X error <= delta_x and chi is L_chi-Lipschitz on support, error is <= sqrt(n)L_chi delta_x. To reserve epsilon_num take delta_chi<=epsilon_num/sqrt(n), delta_x<=epsilon_num/(L_chi sqrt(n)); bit depth also requires support/output ranges and arithmetic model. Constants C0 and C_* are non-effective in the sources, so no numerical n threshold or end-to-end bit complexity follows.

claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the conditional theorem's inherited BTM proof chain or a family satisfying the exact displayed assumptions for which n W2^2/[min(d,k)(log(ed))^8 G8+k] is unbounded refutes the bound. Separately, failure to derive the positive-kappa moment substitution with constants uniform in d kills this reconstruction.
